metadata.description: One grouping's recorded permission for another to use resources it holds — who granted, who received, which resources, what may be done, and until when. Usually two tenants, which is the case CTX-001 depends on and revocation and expiry act on; the record itself is boundary-agnostic because any grouping can declare isolation. A grant permits use and never transfers ownership.

provider_ref.description: The auth-capability provider that evaluates this expression (cardinality-1 URF).

expression.description: OPAQUE provider-scoped subject expression — an LDAP DN, an OIDC claim, a K8s subject. Never parsed or evaluated by UDLM.

subject_bindings.description: The RBAC bridge: external subject-expressions whose holders this grouping is FOR. Opaque by design — parsing or evaluating one would re-import the permission engine the model excludes.

membership_criterion.description: The RULE that derives the member set — a stored URF filter (identifier-scheme 9; declared fields only, URF-005), never the set itself. Idioms: tenancy "estate?tenant_uuid=={self}" (exclusivity is structural — the field is scalar); ownership "estate?owned_by=={self}"; labels "estate?labels.concern==payments"; explicit set "estate?uuid=in=(a,b)" — the marked exception, prefer any derivable form; exclusion "estate?tenant_uuid==abc;member_of!=access/groupings/hold".

obligations.description: Unit-level requirements the engine enforces over the derived set — physical: stores and placement partition by this grouping's uuid (IdP group -> binding -> this anchor -> tenant_uuid -> partitioned stores; every hop on existing machinery).

granted_by.description: The grouping that holds the resources and is giving permission — a Grouping.Tenant in the common case, any isolating grouping in general. A grant across a grouping that declares `obligations.isolation: none` permits nothing, because nothing was closed.

granted_to.description: The grouping whose members receive permission. MUST differ from the granting grouping — a grant to yourself is not a grant, and the boundary it would cross does not exist.

authorized_operations.description: What the receiving grouping's members may do with the resources this grant scopes. `stake` takes a share of a shareable resource; `allocate` carves an owned portion from a pool; `read` sees declared fields without using it. Ownership is never among them — a grant permits use, never transfer.

valid_from.description: When the grant takes effect. Absent means immediately on creation.

expires_at.description: When the grant lapses. Expiry is treated exactly as explicit revocation (CTX-003): dependent entities enter review, and nothing is seized. Absent means the grant runs until revoked — #406 argues that is the wrong default and proposes bounding it, which this element makes addressable.

platform_managed.description:
Set when a platform administrator created this grant on a grouping's behalf rather than the granting grouping creating it itself (CTX-004). It is visible to that grouping, not only to the administrator (CTX-007) — a grant made in your name is one you can audit.
On the record rather than derived from the audit because revocation acts on it: a platform-managed grant notifies the platform administrator as well as both groupings (§13.4), and an operation should not have to walk the audit chain to know who to tell. WHO created the grant is a different question and is NOT here — the audit record requires actor, subject, and action on every act, and that is history rather than something an operation acts on (ADR-059).

context.purpose: One grouping permitting another to use something it holds. The grant is a record with its own identity and lifecycle, so it can be found, audited, time-bounded, and withdrawn.
context.plain_description: Permission for the members of one grouping to use resources held by another — who granted it, who received it, which resources, what they may do, and until when. Usually two tenants; the same record covers any pair of groupings that isolate. Withdrawing it does not seize anything: every dependent entity moves to review, and a human or policy decides whether to re-authorize, release, or migrate.
use_when: A relationship needs to cross a boundary that is otherwise closed — most often two tenants
A shared resource is used by a grouping that does not hold it
An allocation is carved from a pool another grouping holds
Members of a federation share resources while staying independent
not_for: Deciding who may act inside a tenant — external RBAC owns that (ADR-008)
Resource types that waive the per-grant requirement by standing declaration (`publicly_stakeable` / `publicly_allocatable`, CTX-008) — those need no grant at all
Ownership transfer. A grant never moves ownership; it permits use
works_with: Grouping.Tenant — the usual pair of boundaries a grant spans
The required-grant set (CTX-005) — derived from a request's edges and diffed against these
